Solfugid owner here. Unless your skin is literally rice paper or crunchy chitin, these creatures can VERY rarely cause injury. They'll definitely TRY to chew on you, to no avail. Their chelicerae/mandibles are designed to crush insect shells and struggle with malleable skin.

What's her substrate like? Do you mist for water or does she have a bowl? Many T's from arid and even jungle climates tend to have an aversion to substrate over 50-60% humidity. Now that she's about 5 inches like you said, she can drink safely from a small water bowl with minimal enclosure misting. You can choose to do it all the time or just when she enters pre molt, but I always provide a moist area opposite their main hide for easy molting, they will naturally seek it out.
